_comment: Prepared, not run (#11's own text: 'Publish conformance evidence for both collections and a bounded compatibility statement; do not build a second large benchmark'). Execution needs a --subject flag that materializes the named subject through materialize.py, installs it via DockerBackend.install() into a real container, observes discovery via the client's own no-model listing (the same codex debug prompt-input path skillc/exposure.py already uses), and re-verifies an in-container digest against the installation receipt - never a model call. PR #97 (skillc demo --subject <name>) carries an earlier, host-materialize-only shape today: --subject already selects and installs the named subject on the HOST via materialize.materialize(), but does not yet install into the real container, run discovery there, or re-verify a digest. That fuller behavior is a follow-up PR under #11. #81's lifecycle and grading demos are unaffected either way: slug-small-fix stays the graded task regardless of --subject. Neither the follow-up PR nor #10's own live Docker run exists yet.

acceptance_status._comment: The no-agent demo this manifest prepares gives per-collection INSTALLATION and DISCOVERY conformance against a real daemon - an in-container digest check against the receipt, plus the client's own listing. It does NOT satisfy bullet 2, which needs an agent actually working the Level 1 task with each collection installed - a real model call this manifest deliberately never makes.
acceptance_status.bullet_1_selection_provenance_license: MET - evals/subjects/mattpocock-skills/SUBJECT.md (#71/#11): independently authored, different layout, compatible capability scope, provenance and licence recorded
acceptance_status.bullet_2_same_client_fixture_contract_gr: NOT MET by this manifest alone - the harness now exists (skillc collection-run <subject>, skillc/collection_conformance.py, built and proven against the fake docker CLI in tests/test_collection_conformance.py: installs each collection's declared, selected skill files into the SAME container as one agent_trial.run_one_attempt against evals/level1/slug-small-fix, skill-free canary mode, then grades through a separate backend instance), but the actual agent working the task with each collection installed is still owed to the operator's own live run - a real model call this repository's own tests deliberately never make. Funding basis (quoted verbatim from the operator's ruling on #98): "Normal Claude and codex" - the operator's own normal Claude Code and Codex subscription logins, inside the normal usage budget, NOT metered API spend and NOT gated by the #12 $5 cost stop (that ruling covers judge calls only, e.g. mcp-second-opinion, which use provider API keys). The subscription-credential injection into a trial container this needs is delivered under #98 (skillc/credential.py, docker_backend.DockerBackend.deliver_home_file/read_home_file); the agent run itself is not.
acceptance_status.bullet_3_no_branch_refused_before_select: MET - tests/test_materialize.py's genericity guard (CORE_MODULES, an open set since #94) and test_a_malformed_subject_declaration_is_refused's 10 parametrized cases; cited, not re-proven here
acceptance_status.bullet_4_conformance_evidence_and_compat: PARTIALLY MET - this manifest's own runs, once executed, give installation+discovery conformance evidence for both collections through a real daemon; the compatibility statement below is bounded to state exactly that scope, not more
acceptance_status.what_remains_after_this_manifest_s_own_r: ONE item: the operator's own live agent run of `skillc collection-run <subject>`, once per collection, on evals/level1/slug-small-fix - a real model call on the operator's subscription login (see bullet 2). The harness itself (skillc/collection_conformance.py) is built and proven against the fake docker; the credential mechanism it needs is delivered under #98. #11 stays open until the operator's real agent run happens; this manifest's own runs, and the harness now existing, do not close it by themselves.

bounded_compatibility_statement: See README.md in this directory for the full statement, which keeps three kinds of claim separate: executed evidence (materialize.py has actually run against both subjects on the host), static proof (trial.py/verify.py/backend.py/docker_backend.py carry no subject-name branch, never demonstrated by execution), and what remains unshown by either - a full trial (plan, dispatch, capture, grade) for either subject through any backend, AND an agent actually working Level 1 with either collection installed (bullet 2, a real model call). This manifest's own two runs, once executed, close the first gap (installation+discovery through a real daemon) but not the second - #11 stays open until an agent run happens, on the operator's normal Claude Code/Codex subscription login per the ruling quoted on #98 ("Normal Claude and codex"), not metered spend and not gated by the #12 cost stop (that covers judge calls only). The credential-injection mechanism this needs is delivered under #98; the agent run itself is not. This says NOTHING about which collection helps an agent more, about task outcomes, or about any paid model call already having happened.
